title: Universal finite-change sets and strictness

based_on.title: Turing Degrees And The Ershov Hierarchy
based_on.pages: §2.1, printed p.2, Definition 2.2 and the finite set-hierarchy strictness statement; detailed bounded simulator developed explicitly

based_on.title: How to approximate fuzzy sets: mind-changes and the Ershov Hierarchy
based_on.pages: Article 55; The Classical Ershov Hierarchy, Definition 3 and universal-set paragraph preceding Theorem 3

summary: Build a universal problem for each finite revision allowance, then diagonalize to prove that every additional allowed change enlarges the class.
abstract: Programs proposed as membership guesses may stop answering or revise their answers too often. A bounded simulator can still turn every program index into a valid approximation with a prescribed revision allowance, while preserving the limiting answers of every valid candidate. Coding all its rows into one set gives a universal membership problem for that allowance: each problem with the same bound translates into it by an injective computable map. Reversing its diagonal answers then produces a set requiring one additional permitted revision. This proves that the finite change classes grow strictly at every level, including the step from no revisions to one, without requiring an algorithm that recognizes valid approximation programs.
